claim.clinicalNotes:
DATE OF VISIT: 2026-09-24. New patient, sleep medicine consult. Visit conducted in Mandarin with a certified medical interpreter.
HPI: 71-year-old female referred by cardiology for loud snoring, witnessed apneas reported by her daughter, nocturnal awakenings with gasping, and morning headaches for over 1 year. Epworth Sleepiness Scale 14/24. STOP-BANG score 6.
COMORBIDITIES: Chronic systolic heart failure, NYHA class III, ejection fraction 30% on echocardiogram dated 2026-06-11. Moderate-to-severe COPD (FEV1 42% predicted on spirometry 2026-05-20) on continuous home oxygen 2 L/min by nasal cannula. Overnight oximetry on 2026-08-30 showed periodic desaturations with a cyclical pattern; cardiology raised concern for Cheyne-Stokes respiration.
EXAM: BMI 31. Neck circumference 39 cm. Mallampati class IV. Bilateral lower-extremity edema 1+. Lungs with diffuse expiratory wheeze.
ASSESSMENT: High pretest probability of obstructive sleep apnea, with suspected coexisting central sleep apnea (Cheyne-Stokes pattern) in the setting of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Significant cardiopulmonary disease (CHF, moderate-to-severe COPD on supplemental oxygen) makes an unattended home sleep apnea test inappropriate: HSAT cannot reliably detect central apneas, cannot titrate oxygen, and may underestimate disease in patients with chronic hypoxemia.
PLAN: Attended in-laboratory polysomnography (CPT 95810) to characterize obstructive versus central events and guide therapy (CPAP versus adaptive servo-ventilation is contraindicated with EF of 30% or less, so accurate characterization is required). Home sleep apnea test is not appropriate for this patient.
